requirements.subject: ent:predefined-function
requirements.canonical: Annex C IS the normative definition of the TTCN-3 predefined functions.
requirements.original: This annex defines the TTCN-3 predefined functions.

requirements.subject: ent:predefined-function
requirements.condition: the general restrictions of clause 16.1.2 are not met
requirements.canonical: If the general restrictions for predefined functions specified in clause 16.1.2 are not met, the use of the predefined function SHALL cause a compile-time or runtime error.
requirements.original: When the general restrictions specified in clause 16.1.2 are not met, this shall cause a compile time or runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:predefined-function
requirements.condition: no explicit exception-handling rule is defined for the error situation
requirements.canonical: An error situation of a predefined function for which no explicit exception-handling rule is defined in Annex C SHALL cause a compile-time or runtime error.
requirements.original: Error situations for which no explicit exception-handling rule is defined in the relevant clauses of this annex shall cause a TTCN-3 compile-time or runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool MAY decide whether an error situation of a predefined function causes a compile-time error or a runtime error.
requirements.original: Which error situation causes compile-time and which one runtime error is a tool implementation option.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2char
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2char` has the signature `int2char(in integer invalue) return charstring`.
requirements.original: int2char(in integer invalue) return charstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2char
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2char` converts an integer value in the range 0 to 127 into a single-character-length charstring value.
requirements.original: This function converts an integer value in the range of 0 to 127 (8-bit encoding) into a single-character-length charstring value.

ambiguity.issue: The range 0..127 corresponds to a 7-bit character code; the text calls it an 8-bit encoding.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2char
requirements.canonical: The integer value passed to `int2char` IS the encoding (character code) of the resulting character.
requirements.original: The integer value describes the 8-bit encoding of the character.

ambiguity.issue: The range 0..127 corresponds to a 7-bit character code; the text calls it an 8-bit encoding.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2char
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2char`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2char
requirements.canonical: If `invalue` is less than 0 or greater than 127, the call of `int2char` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: invalue is less than 0 or greater than 127. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2unichar
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2unichar` has the signature `int2unichar(in integer invalue) return universal charstring`.
requirements.original: int2unichar(in integer invalue) return universal charstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2unichar
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2unichar` converts an integer value in the range 0 to 2147483647 into a single-character-length universal charstring value.
requirements.original: This function converts an integer value in the range of 0 to 2 147 483 647 (32-bit encoding) into a single-character-length universal charstring value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2unichar
requirements.canonical: The integer value passed to `int2unichar` IS the 32-bit encoding (character code) of the resulting character.
requirements.original: The integer value describes the 32-bit encoding of the character.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2unichar
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2unichar`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2unichar
requirements.canonical: If `invalue` is less than 0 or greater than 2147483647, the call of `int2unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: invalue is less than 0 or greater than 2147483647. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2bit` has the signature `int2bit(in integer invalue, in integer length) return bitstring`.
requirements.original: int2bit(in integer invalue, in integer length) return bitstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2bit` converts a single integer value into a single bitstring value.
requirements.original: This function converts a single integer value to a single bitstring value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: The bitstring returned by `int2bit` IS exactly `length` bits long.
requirements.original: The resulting string is length bits long.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: For the conversion performed by `int2bit`, a bitstring SHALL be interpreted as a positive base 2 integer value.
requirements.original: For the purposes of this conversion, a bitstring shall be interpreted as a positive base 2 integer value.

ambiguity.issue: The value 0 is a valid result/argument, so the bitstring is interpreted as a non-negative (not strictly positive) integer.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2bit`, the rightmost bit IS the least significant bit.
requirements.original: The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2bit`, the leftmost bit IS the most significant bit.
requirements.original: The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2bit`, the bits 0 and 1 represent the decimal values 0 and 1 respectively.
requirements.original: The bits 0 and 1 represent the decimal values 0 and 1 respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.condition: the conversion yields fewer bits than length
requirements.canonical: If the conversion yields fewer bits than specified by the `length` parameter, `int2bit` SHALL pad the resulting bitstring on the left with zeros.
requirements.original: If the conversion yields a value with fewer bits than specified in the length parameter, then the bitstring shall be padded on the left with zeros.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2bit`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.canonical: If `invalue` is less than zero, the call of `int2bit` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more bits than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2bit
requirements.condition: the result needs more than length bits
requirements.canonical: If the conversion yields a return value with more bits than specified by `length`, the call of `int2bit` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more bits than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2enum
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2enum` has the signature `int2enum(in integer inpar, out Enumerated_type outpar)` and has no return value.
requirements.original: int2enum ( in integer inpar, out Enumerated_type outpar)

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2enum
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2enum` converts an integer value into an enumerated value of a given enumerated type.
requirements.original: This function converts an integer value into an enumerated value of a given enumerated type.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2enum
requirements.canonical: The integer value to be converted by `int2enum` SHALL be provided as the `in` parameter `inpar`.
requirements.original: The integer value shall be provided as in parameter and the result of the conversion shall be stored in an out parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2enum
requirements.canonical: The result of the conversion performed by `int2enum` SHALL be stored in the `out` parameter `outpar`.
requirements.original: The integer value shall be provided as in parameter and the result of the conversion shall be stored in an out parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2enum
requirements.canonical: The type of the actual parameter passed to the `out` parameter `outpar` of `int2enum` determines the enumerated type into which `inpar` is converted.
requirements.original: The type of the out parameter determines the type into which the in parameter is converted.

improper_terms.proper: actual parameter passed to the out formal parameter

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'the type of the out parameter'; the formal parameter type is the generic Enumerated_type, so the type of the actual parameter is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter passed to `outpar` of `int2enum` SHALL be a variable of an enumerated type.
requirements.original: The type of the out parameter determines the type into which the in parameter is converted. int2enum ( in integer inpar, out Enumerated_type outpar)

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2enum
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2enum`.
requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

readings: If `inpar` does not equal the integer value associated with any enumerated value of the type of `outpar`, the call of `int2enum` SHALL cause an error (C.0, no explicit exception-handling rule).
If `inpar` does not equal the integer value associated with any enumerated value of the type of `outpar`, `int2enum` SHALL NOT cause an error and `outpar` remains unchanged or unbound.
ambiguity.issue: No error cause is listed for an integer that has no associated enumerated value; the canonical text only restates the general error causes. Reading 1 (error via C.0) is the most likely.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2hex` has the signature `int2hex(in integer invalue, in integer length) return hexstring`.
requirements.original: int2hex(in integer invalue, in integer length) return hexstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2hex` converts a single integer value into a single hexstring value.
requirements.original: This function converts a single integer value to a single hexstring value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: The hexstring returned by `int2hex` IS exactly `length` hexadecimal digits long.
requirements.original: The resulting string is length hexadecimal digits long.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: For the conversion performed by `int2hex`, a hexstring SHALL be interpreted as a positive base 16 integer value.
requirements.original: For the purposes of this conversion, a hexstring shall be interpreted as a positive base 16 integer value.

ambiguity.issue: The value 0 is a valid result/argument, so the hexstring is interpreted as a non-negative (not strictly positive) integer.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2hex`, the rightmost hexadecimal digit IS the least significant digit.
requirements.original: The rightmost hexadecimal digit is least significant, the leftmost hexadecimal digit is the most significant.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2hex`, the leftmost hexadecimal digit IS the most significant digit.
requirements.original: The rightmost hexadecimal digit is least significant, the leftmost hexadecimal digit is the most significant.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2hex`, the hexadecimal digits 0 to F represent the decimal values 0 to 15 respectively.
requirements.original: The hexadecimal digits 0 to F represent the decimal values 0 to 15 respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.condition: the conversion yields fewer hexadecimal digits than length
requirements.canonical: If the conversion yields fewer hexadecimal digits than specified by the `length` parameter, `int2hex` SHALL pad the resulting hexstring on the left with zeros.
requirements.original: If the conversion yields a value with fewer hexadecimal digits than specified in the length parameter, then the hexstring shall be padded on the left with zeros.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2hex`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.canonical: If `invalue` is less than zero, the call of `int2hex` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more hexadecimal characters than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2hex
requirements.condition: the result needs more than length hexadecimal digits
requirements.canonical: If the conversion yields a return value with more hexadecimal digits than specified by `length`, the call of `int2hex` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more hexadecimal characters than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

ambiguity.issue: The error cause uses 'hexadecimal characters' while the rest of the clause uses 'hexadecimal digits'.
